evidence.reference_title: GPSM2 mutations cause the brain malformations and hearing loss in Chudley-McCullough syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Although not always reported in the literature, frontal polymicrogyria and gray matter heterotopia are uniformly present, whereas cerebellar dysplasia, ventriculomegaly, and arachnoid cysts are nearly invariant.

evidence.reference_title: GPSM2 mutations cause the brain malformations and hearing loss in Chudley-McCullough syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Although not always reported in the literature, frontal polymicrogyria and gray matter heterotopia are uniformly present, whereas cerebellar dysplasia, ventriculomegaly, and arachnoid cysts are nearly invariant.

nodes.description: Hearing aids gave limited benefit in a six-patient series, and all patients eventually received cochlear implants, with satisfactory aided thresholds but variable speech recognition.

evidence.reference_title: Hearing loss and cochlear implantation in Chudley McCullough syndrome: A case series.
evidence.snippet: Cochlear implantation emerged as the optimal treatment, demonstrating superiority over hearing aid rehabilitation to improve hearing performance.

nodes.description: GPSM2 orients the mitotic spindle of dividing neural progenitors. Loss of spindle-orientation control changes the plane of progenitor division, which shifts the balance between progenitor types and alters cortical growth. This is the proposed basis of the cortical and callosal malformations; it has not been shown directly in patient brain.
nodes.id: Defective Mitotic Spindle Orientation in Neural Progenitors

evidence.reference_title: Oriented cell divisions induce basal progenitors and regulate neural expansion across tissues and species.
evidence.snippet: We show here that double inactivation of spindle orientation regulators GPSM2 and SAPCD2 in mice completely reorients progenitor divisions in both the neocortex and retina.

nodes.description: Stereocilia of auditory and vestibular hair cells fail to elongate, and the hair bundle loses its graded staircase architecture and can be misoriented, so mechanotransduction is impaired.
nodes.id: Defective Stereocilia Elongation and Hair Bundle Morphogenesis

evidence.reference_title: Defective Gpsm2/Gα(i3) signalling disrupts stereocilia development and growth cone actin dynamics in Chudley-McCullough syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that mutation of the mouse orthologue of GPSM2 affects actin-rich stereocilia elongation in auditory and vestibular hair cells, causing deafness and balance defects.

evidence.reference_title: The GPSM2/LGN GoLoco motifs are essential for hearing.
evidence.snippet: Lgn (ΔC) mice, with a targeted deletion truncating the C-terminal GoLoco motifs, are profoundly deaf and show misorientation of the hair bundle and severe malformations in stereocilia shape that deteriorates over time.

nodes.description: Speech delay secondary to the hearing loss. When the hearing loss is managed early, motor and cognitive development is usually normal or only mildly affected.

evidence.reference_title: Chudley-McCullough Syndrome: A Recognizable Clinical Entity Characterized by Deafness and Typical Brain Malformations.
evidence.snippet: We report 2 cases of Chudley-McCullough syndrome, one presenting with congenital deafness and normal development except for speech delay

evidence.snippet: When hearing loss is managed early, most patients have minor or no impairment of motor and cognitive development, despite the presence of brain malformations.

evidence.reference_title: Whole exome sequencing and homozygosity mapping identify mutation in the cell polarity protein GPSM2 as the cause of nonsyndromic hearing loss DFNB82.
evidence.snippet: The nonsense mutation leads to an early truncation of the G protein signaling modulator GPSM2, a protein that is essential for maintenance of cell polarity and spindle orientation.

evidence.reference_title: GPSM2 mutations cause the brain malformations and hearing loss in Chudley-McCullough syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Subsequent brain imaging of these individuals revealed frontal polymicrogyria, abnormal corpus callosum, and gray matter heterotopia, consistent with a CMS diagnosis, but no ventriculomegaly.

nodes.description: Biallelic truncating variants (nonsense, frameshift and canonical splice site) remove GPSM2 function. Most truncate the protein before or within the C-terminal GoLoco motifs that bind GNAI, so the GPSM2-GNAI complex cannot form.

evidence.reference_title: GPSM2 mutations cause the brain malformations and hearing loss in Chudley-McCullough syndrome.
evidence.snippet: revealed four molecular variations (two single-base deletions, a nonsense mutation, and a canonical splice-site mutation) in the G protein-signaling modulator 2 gene, GPSM2, that underlie CMS

evidence.reference_title: A novel nonsense GPSM2 mutation in a Yemeni family underlying Chudley-McCullough syndrome.
evidence.snippet: This mutation is predicted to abolish all four GoLoco domains in GPSM2 and this explains the bioinformatic prediction for this mutation to be functionally damaging.

nodes.description: Gpsm2 mutant mice are deaf and have balance defects, with failed stereocilia elongation in auditory and vestibular hair cells.
Hydrocephalus, often from obstruction at the foramen of Monro, sometimes needing a shunt. It varies even between siblings with the same variant.

evidence.reference_title: Chudley-McCullough syndrome: expanded phenotype and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Chudley-McCullough syndrome is an autosomal recessive condition characterized by profound sensorineural deafness, hydrocephalus secondary to obstruction of the foramen of Monro, and other structural abnormalities of the brain.

evidence.reference_title: Chudley-McCullough Syndrome: Variable Clinical Picture in Twins with a Novel GPSM2 Mutation.
evidence.snippet: While one child developed hydrocephalus-prompting shunt implantation immediately after birth, the other sibling did not.

nodes.description: In mouse neurons lacking Gpsm2, growth cone outgrowth is reduced and actin dynamics are disrupted. Its contribution to the human malformations, including the callosal defect, has not been established.
nodes.id: Impaired Neuronal Growth Cone Actin Dynamics

evidence.reference_title: Defective Gpsm2/Gα(i3) signalling disrupts stereocilia development and growth cone actin dynamics in Chudley-McCullough syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Our results elucidate the aetiology of CMCS and highlight a new molecular role for Gpsm2/Gαi3 in the regulation of actin dynamics in epithelial and neuronal tissues.

nodes.description: In wild-type hair cells, GPSM2 and GNAI are recruited to the tips of the first, tallest row of stereocilia, where they join a MYO15A-whirlin-EPS8 tip complex and give that row its identity. Without GPSM2, the complex does not form and the bundle keeps an immature organization.
nodes.id: Loss of the GPSM2-GNAI Stereocilia Tip Complex

evidence.reference_title: GPSM2-GNAI Specifies the Tallest Stereocilia and Defines Hair Bundle Row Identity.
evidence.snippet: We discovered that WHRN-GPSM2-GNAI is an extra module recruited by and added to a pre-existing MYO15A-EPS8 stereocilia tip complex. This extended complex is only present in the first, tallest row

evidence.reference_title: Promotion of row 1-specific tip complex condensates by Gpsm2-Gαi provides insights into row identity of the tallest stereocilia.
evidence.snippet: A deafness-associated mutation of Gpsm2 leads to impaired formation of the 5xTCD condensates and consequently reduced actin bundling, providing possible clues for etiology of hearing loss in patients with Chudley-McCullough syndrome.

nodes.description: The brain malformations of the syndrome: frontal polymicrogyria, subcortical heterotopia, partial agenesis of the corpus callosum and cerebellar dysplasia.
